# Who Checks the Government?

<!-- STEP id="loop-starts" -->
## Answering to Citizens

A government must answer to citizens for how it uses power. This is called **accountability**.

Citizens judge its actions through elections, public debates and civil society, and this builds trust.

<!-- STEP id="question-hour-audit" -->
## Question Hour and the Audit

**Question Hour** is the first hour of a parliamentary session, when members ask the government questions. This helps check the government's work.

Government accounts are also audited, or checked, so spending can be examined.

<!-- STEP id="transparency-tools" -->
## The Right to Know

**Transparency** means that people can see how the government works. Citizens can seek information under the **RTI Act, 2005**.

Four bodies also help: the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), the Central Information Commission (CIC), the Lokpal and the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). Tap each name.
